system.notes: Some values disagree between Tomokiyo's table and the cribs (his b=u, m=r, 8=c; cribs give p, o, t); in fr. 4715 plain m is r, in no. 62 tailed m is o. Signs are letter-shaped glyphs, digits and graphic signs; symbol_kind approximates this mix. 22 Sept: 41 distinct signs in no. 62 (measured). Homophones confirmed: n = ◻/Ħ/H, o = tt/m(tailed)/⋕, m = ∇/x, e = θ/æ, i = 9/ħ/ɸ, u/v = ɔ/φ/b. Codes: ⌘ = Mr, Ƒ = le, n = et, ʃ = jay, 1 = de.

solution.what: Fetched fr. 3413 no. 62 and the three bound keys (nos. 53, 61, 69) from Gallica.
Tested the three bound keys: no. 53 numeric (letter has no figures), no. 61 Italian with other signs, no. 69 gives square = e where the letter needs n.
Tomokiyo's nevers.htm identifies the Nevers-Piles cipher and reads 'Cassin'; his partial table confirms W V ÷ 9 ◻ = Cassin.
Cribs from the clear context: 'la protection', 'vostre', signature b-a-r-o-? (Baron).
Annealed unread glyphs in their clear-text context under a French 6-gram LM (solve.py); groups too short, only the signature 'baron' stabilises.
Aligned BnF fr. 4715 f. 2 (same cipher, interlinear decipherment) word by word: confirms 4=h, 3=d, 1=de, ∇=m, += l and adds 7=d, z=b, H=n, δ=t, q=s, g=i.
With the added values: 'depeschera', '[code] mon maitre a esté retiré', 'vostre regne'; groups C, H, I and code signs ⌘ Ƒ τ ʃ unread.
Fetched fr. 3413 ff. 126-127 and fr. 4715 ff. 2r-v at full IIIF resolution from Gallica; fr. 3612 checked again on Gallica SRU: not digitised.
Re-transcribed the 14 cipher runs of no. 62 at native resolution into no62_cipher.txt (91 signs, measured). Corrections: S1 sign is θ not Ⱥ; G sign after x is ⋕ not tt; signature ends Ħ (= n).

Viewed all 29 cipher lines of fr. 4715 f. 2 and aligned ~50 words with the interlinear (fr4715_f2_aligned.txt): adds ʃ = jay, ʃ-with-bar = le, x = m, tailed m = o, a = f, n = et, ⋕ = n, o = p, d = x, ω = a, Δ = z. Full sign-by-sign transcription not completed.
Re-read Tomokiyo's nevers.htm and his Nevers-Piles table image: ⌘ = Mr, n = et, Ⱥ = f, ħ-form = i, b = u.
S2 = 'le doien'; G = 'Mr le [τ] mon maistre'; H = "j'ay veu ung advis"; I = 'confirme' (constrained word search ranks it highest among sense readings); signature Baron confirmed.
Constrained word search over C, I and V2 with the extended key (fr-gutenberg lexicon, up to 2 broken values).
Old guesses tested against the extended key: V2 gives et-f-e-g-n-e, so 'regne'/'Champaigne' fail; C gives v-o-p-a-e-?-s, no sense.
Re-checked C, V2 and the code signs at native resolution: V2 fifth sign is dotted ⊡ (r), not ◻; C sixth sign is the small ʃ = y of fr. 4715; C last sign = ÷.

Added an LM sense test (fr-1600-letters, per-char threshold -4.0) to decode62.py; it agrees with all hand flags. C = v-o-p-a-e-y-s and V2 = et-f-e-g-r-e fail; 'vos pays' and '… gré' are context guesses, not counted.
Lexicon search for patterns ??egre, ???gre, vo?pa??s, ?o?a??s; nothing fits both the values and the context.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): cipher groups no62_cipher.txt; decode62.py output saved as texts/no62_decryption.md; key copied from decode62.py to texts/key.md; the clear text of the letter is not transcribed

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/no62_decryption.md is one line per cipher group with no clear text around it; the groups read as words but no sentence can be built. Per-document D confirmed; no. 62 relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read; method read with known key -> not solved; fraction_read 0.824 -> 0.

no. 62: Gallica views 259-262 fetched at full resolution (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF); the clear text of ff. 126r-127r transcribed for the first time and the fourteen cipher runs set in their clauses (texts/no62_reading.md, English texts/no62_en.md). f. 127v is the address leaf only (no cipher in the bleed-through).

Runs C ('pour ce qui touche [C]') and V2 ('vous serez a vostre [V2] si l'histoire est vraye') retried in full clear context (vos amis, vos pays, abbaye, Champaigne): each needs two or more values against the key. Unread.

no. 62 reading scored: 0.882 (45/51) plain, 1.0 explicit holes only; six of the seven cipher-bearing sentences hold; look-alike letters 0. decoded, not read -> read (B); class not read -> read in part (C, V2 and three code signs open, no key material); method back to read with known key; fraction_read 0 -> 1.

Consistency pass (cl): the closed item (no. 62 as a running text) was still a bullet in NOTES Remaining gaps, which the checker reads as an open gap without a blocker; restated below the list as Closed. outcome.gaps unchanged (it already lists only the open pieces).

texts.label: Letter to the abbé d'Orbais, Rome, 23 Aug [1589], BnF fr. 3413 no. 62
texts.summary: A secretary of Cardinal Pellevé, signing Baron, writes from Rome to Jean de Piles, abbé d'Orbais, the League's envoy, with the news of Henri III's death: couriers from Spain, Genoa and Tuscany, and the Duke of Lorraine's letter from his agent Bardin in Paris, 8 August ('le Roy a esté tué, et c'est le Roy de Navarre qui l'a faict faire'; the Cardinal de Bourbon proclaimed King in Paris). In cipher: '[Ƃ] depeschera [ʃ] dedans deux jours le doien', 'la protection que vous sçavez', Mons. Cassin (his senior, ill with fever), 'Mr le [τ] mon maistre', 'j'ay veu ung advis qui confirme', the signature Baron.

reading_review.note: texts/no62_reading.md: the clear text of ff. 126r-127r transcribed from the Gallica images (first time) with the fourteen cipher runs set in their clauses, read with the extended Nevers-Piles key of decode62.py. Reading body 0.882 (45/51) plain, 1.0 explicit holes only; of the seven sentences that carry cipher, six hold (the S1 sentence has two code holes). Look-alike letters 0. Open: run C ('ce qui touche [...]'), run V2 ('vous serez a vostre [...]') and the code signs Ƃ, ʃ, τ (no key material).
